Subject: Questions on auto-renew and termination notice windows

Marcus —

Quick question from procurement as we move to finalize the MSA: Jordan Tech is interpreting the current draft as automatic renewals for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives 30 days notice before renewal. We typically require a 60-day notice for auto-renew avoidance. Also, our legal lead is pushing back on a broad termination-for-convenience right with only 30 days notice — they prefer 90 days or a mutual termination mechanism.

Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility here? If we can land on a clean set of notice windows (auto-renew notice, exit for convenience, and any early termination fees), procurement can proceed to internal approval this week.

Thanks,

Lisa — thanks for flagging. We understand procurement timelines and want to land on something that keeps both sides comfortable. High level proposal from my side:

- Term and auto-renew: 12 month initial term with automatic 12 month renewals unless either party gives 60 days prior written notice before the renewal date.
- Termination for convenience: allow either party to terminate with 90 days prior written notice. No early termination fee if notice is respected.

I attached a redline with the changes called MSA_Redline_v3.docx that updates Sections 2 (Term), 2.3 (Auto-Renew), and 8 (Termination). There is also a short notice matrix (see attached Notice_Matrix.xlsx) that spells out effective dates depending on countersign dates.

If legal wants alternative wording (for example: 90 days only applies to customer-initiated termination; vendor to retain a shorter customer-initiated window), loop Neha and Markus in and we can quantify the tradeoffs. Happy to jump on a 20 minute call to close.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: proposed legal language for term/renewal/termination

Team — quick draft language below for Marcus to send to Jordan Tech. I think this strikes the right commercial balance and reduces downstream ambiguity. Please review.

Proposed clauses (to insert in Section 2 and Section 8):

1) Term. The Initial Term shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of twelve (12) months ("Initial Term"). Thereafter, the Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month terms (each a "Renewal Term") unless either party gives the other party sixty (60) days prior written notice of non-renewal before the end of the then-current Term.

2) Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days prior written notice to the other party. Termination under this Section shall be without liability for termination fees provided the terminating party complies with the notice requirement.

3) Early Termination Remedies. Termination for material breach and termination for convenience are distinct. If Customer terminates for convenience within the first six (6) months of the Initial Term, Redwood may invoice for a pro rata minimum commitment equal to the balance of the first six (6) months. Otherwise, no additional termination fee shall apply.

Rationale: 60-day auto-renew notice aligns with procurement cycles. 90-day termination for convenience gives both parties runway to migrate workloads, which is important operationally for us. The limited early-term fee protects against churn within an unproven adoption window.

If you want an alternative (60-day convenience notice instead of 90), we should quantify the concession on pricing or onboarding terms.

Neha
